content: There are two distinct types of talk pages. The first type is the standard talk page, which is specifically designed for discussions related to an article. The second type is the user talk page, which serves as a platform for communication between users or for leaving messages for other users. Every page, with the exception of those in the Special: namespace, has a corresponding talk page. If a page has not yet been discussed, the link to its talk page will appear in red. However, this does not prevent you from initiating a discussion; it simply means you will be the first to do so. To access a talk page, look for a link labeled Talk, Discussion, or Discuss this page. These links are typically located either at the top of the page or on the left-hand side, near the Edit this page option. A talk page is identified by the addition of Talk: at the beginning of the main page's title. If the main page has a prefix, the term Talk is added after the prefix. For instance, a talk page associated with the main article namespace will have the prefix Talk:. Similarly, a talk page associated with the user namespace will have the prefix User talk:. For example, this article is in the Help: namespace, so its talk page is titled Help talk:Talk page. The Main Page, which resides in the main namespace (as it has no prefix), has its talk page titled Talk:Main Page. Additionally, if another user edits your user talk page, an alert stating You have new messages will automatically appear on all pages you view until you visit your user talk page. When using talk pages, it is important to sign your contributions. This can be done by typing three tildes (~~~), which will display your username, or four tildes (~~~~), which will display your username along with a timestamp (e.g., Username 19:36, 10 January 2006 (UTC)). When discussing the name of a page or considering merging it with another page, always explicitly mention the current page name. This is because after renaming (or moving) a page, references to this page name may no longer make sense. On a talk page, the term this page typically refers to the main page associated with the talk page. If you are referring to the talk page itself, it is best to use the term this talk page. The Post a comment feature allows users to conveniently append a new section to a talk page. The section header will automatically match the edit summary, and it only needs to be typed once. This feature can also be used on other pages, although there is no direct link displayed for it. In such cases, you will need to manually use the URL. It is worth noting that the practice of spamming, which involves posting similar messages on multiple users' talk pages—often to solicit a specific action—is strongly discouraged. Proper formatting is essential for maintaining the readability of talk pages, especially given the wide range of formatting options provided by the wiki software platform. The depth of a message in a discussion is determined by the number of colons (':') placed in front of the message. Each colon represents an additional level of indentation, which is commonly used in discussions on both user and article talk pages. When replying to a statement, you should add one more colon than the number used in the statement you are responding to. For example: Original statement: (no colons) Reply: (one colon) Reply to the reply: (two colons) This style of indentation creates a clear and structured flow of conversation, making it easier for users to read and follow discussions.
